title: Lomo Saltado
subtitle: Peruvian beef stir-fry with chips and rice
excerpt: Lomo saltado is a Peruvian stir-fry that combines soy-marinated beef strips with tomatoes, onions and chips, all tossed over fierce heat. It is served alongside white rice for a satisfying double-carb combination. The dish is a product of Peru's chifa culinary tradition, blending Chinese technique with Peruvian ingredients.
sourceNotes: Lomo saltado is one of the most recognisable dishes from Peru's chifa culinary tradition, which blends Peruvian and Chinese cooking. Chinese workers who arrived in Peru in the nineteenth century adapted their stir-fry techniques to local ingredients, creating a genre of cooking now central to Peruvian cuisine.

glossaryTerms.definition: A Peruvian stir-fry dish that blends Chinese cooking techniques with Peruvian ingredients. The name means jumped loin, referring to the way the beef is tossed over high heat.

content.text: This recipe serves 4 and takes around 40 minutes from start to plate.

is one of Peru's most beloved everyday dishes, combining soy-marinated beef with tomato wedges, onions and fried chips, all cooked together in a smoking-hot wok and served with white rice on the side.

The key to this dish is heat. The wok must be as hot as your hob will allow before anything goes in. Work in batches if needed so the beef sears rather than steams. Have everything prepped and beside the hob before you start cooking, because once the wok is hot the whole dish comes together in under 10 minutes.
Cut 600g potatoes into thick chips. Fry in hot oil until golden and cooked through, or toss in oil and bake at 220C for 30 minutes. Season with salt and set aside.
Mix the 2 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp red wine vinegar and 1 tsp aji amarillo paste (if using) in a small bowl. Set aside.
Heat your wok over the highest heat until it begins to smoke. Add 2 tbsp of the vegetable oil and swirl to coat.

Add the beef strips in a single layer. Leave to sear for 1 to 2 minutes without moving, then toss and cook for another minute. The beef should be browned on the outside and still slightly pink inside. Remove to a plate.
Add the remaining oil to the wok. Add the onion wedges and garlic. Stir-fry for 2 minutes until the onion begins to soften at the edges but still holds its shape.
Add the tomato wedges and pour in the soy sauce mixture. Toss everything together and cook for 1 minute. The tomatoes should soften slightly but not collapse.
Return the beef to the wok along with the chips. Toss everything together over high heat for 30 seconds. The chips will absorb some of the sauce.
Remove from the heat. Squeeze over the lime juice and scatter with chopped coriander. Serve immediately with cooked white rice alongside.

attrs.symptom: Beef is grey and steamed rather than browned
attrs.cause: The wok was not hot enough, or the beef was added in too large a batch
attrs.fix: Get the wok smoking before adding oil. Cook the beef in two batches if needed, giving each piece contact with the hot surface.

attrs.cause: They were cooked too long or stirred too vigorously
attrs.fix: Add tomatoes last among the vegetables and cook for no more than 1 minute. Fold gently rather than tossing hard.

attrs.symptom: Chips are soggy after going into the wok
attrs.cause: The chips were added too early or were underdone
attrs.fix: Make sure chips are fully cooked and crisp before adding. Toss them in at the very end and serve immediately.

content.text: Lomo saltado is eaten all over Peru, from home kitchens to busy city restaurants. It is one of those dishes that shows up on almost every Peruvian menu and is cooked just as often on a weeknight as it is for guests.
